Click an option, or Tab to the chosen one and use the arrow keys. The font changes at once, without a reload, and this browser remembers it: on the next visit the app starts with your font already chosen, and other open tabs switch too. Code, ids, and JSON always stay in Geist Mono. The fonts come with the app, so they work offline. The choice is per browser, kept in `localStorage` (`graphgoblin-font`); a private window or blocked site data opens in Geist.

While a font is loading, or if it cannot load, the text it sets shows in the next font in its list and stays usable: Chakra Petch headings and the wordmark show in Geist, and the other fonts, Geist included, show in your system's interface font (Segoe UI on Windows). Text size and spacing settings are not available yet.

## Choose a model and effort

**Enabled in the catalogue** is your selection preference, and **Ready** preflight confirms
prerequisites such as installation and login. Neither proves that your Codex account and provider
endpoint can run every listed model. Shipped model definitions and the bundled CLI's static plan
information do not measure current access. A historical `gpt-5.5` refusal for a ChatGPT login does not establish a current
restriction for every account, or guarantee that switching to an API key would fix it.
If a Codex inference turn's provider message explicitly refuses that model for the account or endpoint, follow
[model-access troubleshooting](07-troubleshooting.md#codex-model-unavailable-for-this-account-or-endpoint)
and make a deliberate supported-model or login/endpoint choice. LLM decisions retain only a safe
provider-failure category, so their run record cannot establish an account-specific cause.

Use the **Enabled** switch in a model's row to enable or disable it. Tab reaches each switch; Space or Enter toggles it. The switch is named **Enable <display name>** and shows **Enabling…** or **Disabling…** with a busy indicator while it saves. It ignores further activation until the request finishes, then announces **Enabled** or **Disabled**. Keyboard focus stays on the switch while saving; moving to another control keeps that focus. A refused request restores its previous state and announces the reason. Disabling a model removes it from new **Default model** choices; enabling it restores the choice. A saved default stays selected as **<name> (disabled)** or **<id> (not in catalog)**, with a diagnostic that it must be corrected before publication or execution. Catalog entries do not prove your account has access.

Harness models offer only the enable switch. Local models served through LiteLLM will appear in the catalog once the LiteLLM adapter is configured. Until local entries exist, **Add model**, **Edit**, and **Delete** are hidden and the catalog names this guide section. With a LiteLLM entry in the list, **Add model** appears and only LiteLLM rows offer **Edit** and **Delete**. Removing a local model leaves its loops referencing that model.

**GPT-6.1 Terra** (`gpt-6.1-terra`) appears enabled when GraphGoblin next starts, with `medium` as its listed catalog default effort and choices from **none (no reasoning)** to `max`. Existing model switches and your saved default model stay as you chose them. Short real Terra turns at `none` and `medium` passed on the bundled Codex CLI 0.160.0; account access is still checked when a run executes. The [delivery evidence](../qa/2026-11-07-issue-440/README.md) records the verified scope. Claude Fable remains Fable 5.1, the latest Fable identity verified in official documentation.

Toggle and model-form refusals use plain sentences: **Harness models can only be enabled or disabled.** (`MODEL_MANAGED_BY_HARNESS`); **LiteLLM is not configured. Adding local models is not available yet.** (`LITELLM_NOT_CONFIGURED`); and **This model is no longer in the catalog.** (`MODEL_NOT_FOUND`). A toggle refused with 404 refreshes the catalog, announces the reason in the section, and focuses its heading if the focused row disappears. LiteLLM creation remains unavailable until the adapter ships.

1	import type { CodexOptions } from '@openai/codex-sdk';
2	import { plainCodexConfigSegment } from '@graphgoblin/contracts';
3	import type { CliCommand, CliRunner } from './cli.js';
4	
5	/**
6	 * Codex turns inherit configured plugins (ADR-0067), with other extensions isolated (ADR-0063).
7	 *
8	 * The CLI loads `~/.codex/config.toml` (and a trusted project's `.codex/config.toml`) for every
9	 * turn. The CLI resolves installed and remote plugins, including their enabled/disabled state
10	 * and their own MCP servers. These defaults still switch off standalone MCP servers, ChatGPT
11	 * apps, memories, goals, sub-agents, lifecycle hooks and the `notify` program.
12	 *
13	 * - `features.<name>=false` switches a feature off; `features.plugins=false` removes every local
14	 *   and remote plugin and the MCP servers they bring.
15	 * - `--config` overrides merge into the loaded tables, so `mcp_servers={}` clears nothing and a
16	 *   non-table value fails the configuration. Each configured server is switched off by name with
17	 *   `mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false`; naming a server that is not configured also fails the
18	 *   configuration, so the names come from the CLI itself (`codex mcp list --json`).
19	 * - Arrays replace, so `notify=[]` removes the turn-completion program.
20	 * - Among repeated `--config` keys the last one wins.
21	 *
22	 * Order of the `--config` arguments: server switches, these defaults, then the node's own
23	 * `configOverrides` (so a node turns one server back on with `mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=true`,
24	 * or opts out of plugins with `features.plugins=false`), then the SDK's thread options, which
25	 * win over overrides of the corresponding keys. Other sandbox-related keys remain separate.
26	 *
27	 * Every key segment that reaches `--config`, a listed server name or a node override key, must be
28	 * one plain TOML key (letters, digits, `_`, `-`) and not `__proto__`, `constructor` or
29	 * `prototype` (QA423-01, review round 1). Anything else refuses the turn before it starts, and
30	 * the configuration is built from prototype-free tables.
31	 */
32	
33	type Config = NonNullable<CodexOptions['config']>;
34	type ConfigValue = Config[string];
35	
36	const isTable = (value: unknown): value is Config =>
37	  typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);

40	export function overrideRefusal(path: string): Error {
41	  return Object.assign(

# Changelog

All notable changes to GraphGoblin. The design is in [docs/](docs/README.md); the user guide is [docs/guide/](docs/guide/README.md).

## Unreleased

- Clarify that an enabled Codex model and a ready preflight do not establish current access
  for the API user's login and provider endpoint. Recognized Codex inference-turn refusals retain
  the provider's explanation; LLM decisions retain only a safe failure category. The guide
  describes deliberate supported-model/login selection without automatic fallback or an
  API-key-only promise (#427).
- Reconcile Codex sandbox documentation and source comments: the authored sandbox permission
  level is explicit, while Windows backend selection remains inherited unless explicitly
  overridden. No sandbox permissions or backend behavior changed (#365).

- Windows launcher identity and ownership checks own their descendants in private Windows jobs
  (#459), drain both output streams within a bounded work window and collect failed checks
  before displaying errors. Initial checks retain the 15-second work cap, with up to two seconds
  for cleanup; held-store retries reserve that cleanup time and retain the last held guidance
  when a conclusive new sample cannot fit. Raw helper output is never displayed or logged.

# ADR-0063 - Loop turns run without the machine's personal extensions

Date: 2026-10-28. Status: accepted (owner decision 2026-10-27, option A; #423).

Update 2026-11-07: [ADR-0067](ADR-0067-codex-inherits-configured-plugins.md) supersedes the Codex plugin-off default and confirms inheritance of ordinary settings, skills and personal instructions (D2). Other isolation defaults and Claude's policy below remain in force. The remainder records the original decision and evidence.

## Context

The final integrated check found every real Codex loop turn starting the machine's own Codex extensions inside the turn's process tree: `node_repl.exe`, plugin MCP servers under `node.exe` and `cmd.exe` ([F2 record](../qa/2026-10-27-final-f2-live/README.md), observation O1). They come from the user's `~/.codex/config.toml`, which the CLI loads for every invocation: `[mcp_servers.*]`, `[plugins.*]` and marketplaces, `[features]` such as `memories` and `apps`, and a `notify` program. [docs/06](../06-harness-integration.md) said per-thread options keep the machine's `config.toml` defaults from leaking into a loop. That held for model, effort, sandbox and approval, not for extensions.

The owner chose option A: loop turns switch off inherited plugins, MCP servers and personal features by default, and a node's existing Codex `configOverrides` stay the way to turn a specific server back on. Option B, a separate Codex home for loops, was not chosen.

## What the pinned CLI allows

Verified on Codex CLI 0.160.0 with dry runs that reach no provider ([WP-423 record](../qa/2026-10-28-wp-423-isolation/README.md)):

- `--config` overrides merge into the loaded tables. `mcp_servers={}`, `plugins={}` and `marketplaces={}` clear nothing; a non-table value such as `mcp_servers=[]` fails the configuration.
- `mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false` switches one server off. Naming a server that is not configured fails the configuration (`invalid transport`), so the names must come from the configuration the CLI actually loads.
- `features.plugins=false` removes every local and remote plugin, the MCP servers they bring and their marketplaces. A single plugin cannot be enabled while the feature is off. `plugins.<id>.enabled` works only unquoted, because the CLI splits `--config` keys on dots.
- `features.<name>=false` switches a feature off. `notify=[]` replaces the configured program; arrays replace rather than merge.
- Among repeated `--config` keys the last one wins.
- `codex mcp list --json` reads the same layers as a turn, including a trusted project's `.codex/config.toml` from its working directory. `codex exec` reads that project layer from `--cd`.
- `codex exec --ignore-user-config` skips `config.toml` entirely, but the SDK has no option for it.

## Decision

Before each Codex turn, the adapter runs `codex mcp list --json` in the turn's working directory, with the turn's CLI and environment and plugins and apps switched off. The turn then starts with these `--config` arguments, in order:

1. `mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false` for every server listed.
2. The isolation defaults: `features.plugins=false`, `features.apps=false`, `features.memories=false`, `features.hooks=false`, `features.multi_agent=false`, `features.goals=false` and `notify=[]`.
3. The node's `harnessOptions.configOverrides`, layered key path by key path, with dotted keys read as paths as the CLI reads them.
4. The SDK's thread options (model, effort, sandbox, approval, network access, web search), which no override can weaken.

The switched-off features bring the machine's installs, account connectors or personal state into a turn, or change what an unattended turn can do:

- installed and remote plugins;
- ChatGPT apps;
- the memory store and goals, both personal state;
- lifecycle hook commands;
- sub-agent spawning (`multi_agent`).

# Working in this repository

GraphGoblin is a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo in TypeScript. Read `docs/README.md` first; `docs/12-implementation-plan.md` says what is being built now and `docs/decisions/` records settled decisions.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.

Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.

Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.

## Rules

- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.

## Commands

On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.

```
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test:coverage
pnpm lint
pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
```

# Targeted correction review 2: A is accepted, B is accepted

I reviewed both correction deltas statically and read-only, using Read, Glob and Grep only. Neither delta adds a misleading claim, and neither has a direct root cause that should block it. The earlier verdicts still stand for the commits they covered: review 1 gave `f96a4073` CHANGES_REQUIRED and gave `b45807f0` APPROVE. These two verdicts cover only the correction deltas.

| Slice | Verdict | Head | Tree (from the brief) | Base (sole parent, from the brief) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: #427/#365 | **ACCEPT CORRECTION** | `8980c27c75e04d33cdcf48736c71db05e35175a3` | `7e23133e3d1f6ffdf49d7d025fc7a15aaf290c54` | `f96a4073c3b53af7724d1ef5593eeaf03194c4cd` |
| B: #448 | **ACCEPT CORRECTION** | `083d7264ffaeaadba44ebd2f929efb4ac526a127` | `485df640b90c94ac9a79bc8fe682b311748dd876` | `b45807f033601a53919f2c9e16e0de751971a518` |

**Checking that the patches match the worktrees:** each branch ref matches its head (`refs/heads/codex/gg-i4-427-guide` holds `8980c27c…` and `codex/gg-i4-448-preflight` holds `083d7264…`). The patches came from `capture-patches.py` (`git diff base head`, which asserts the worktree is clean). The files in each worktree match the added lines in the patches.

## A — #427/#365: ACCEPT CORRECTION

**F1 (decision provider text) is fixed.**
- **CHANGELOG (lines 8–9)** now limits the kept explanation to "Recognized Codex inference-turn refusals" and says "LLM decisions retain only a safe failure category."
- **guide/07 (lines 119 and 135)** limits the diagnosis and the fix to Codex inference turns. The new paragraph at lines 141–146 says the decision records only a safe category, that this category can't establish an account cause, and that the fix is a deliberate supported model followed by a new run. guide/06 (lines 47–50) and docs/06 (lines 509 and 518–521) are limited the same way.
- **The source agrees:**
  - The Codex refusal code becomes `DECIDER_HTTP_ERROR` with no status, and the provider text is dropped (`decider.ts:14-35`).
  - The engine replaces the message with "Decision provider request failed" (`decider-errors.ts:6,24-50`).
  - Without a status the failure can't be resumed, and `details.code` is set (`primitive-evaluator.ts:83-102`).
  - That function is the path LLM decisions take (`primitive-evaluator.ts:288-332`).
  - LLM decisions can only use Codex (`contracts/evaluation.ts:367`, `z.literal('codex')`).
- The rule against keeping provider text is unchanged, and no fallback or coerce policy was added.

**F2 is fixed.**
- **Plan information:** guide/07 (lines 128–129) and guide/06 (lines 44–45) now name the bundled CLI's static plan information and say GraphGoblin's catalogue has no account-plan field. That matches `contracts/catalog.ts:13-22`.
- **Restart step:** added at guide/07 lines 135–136 and docs/06 line 514.
- **`model_not_found`:** removed. Line 123 now says "A generic failure…".
- **Duplicate row:** the existing "Codex rejects the model ID" row (line 166) now links to the new section, and the anchor resolves.

**F3 is fixed in the three named places.**
- docs/06 line 523, `options.ts:90-92` and `isolation.ts:24-25` now say only that each thread setting wins over an override of the same key, and that this doesn't establish what other sandbox keys enforce.
- **The SDK agrees** (`codex-sdk@0.160.0 dist/index.js:178-235`): config overrides are emitted first, followed by `--model`, `--sandbox`, `--cd`, effort, `network_access`, `web_search` and `approval_policy`.
- **The adapter always sends** model, effort, sandbox, approval, network, web search and skip-git (`options.ts:46-60`), plus the working directory when one is set.
- **Comment-only:** both `.ts` changes sit inside `/** */` blocks. The proof that the compiled JS is identical is the root's evidence, not mine.

**Optional wording notes (not blockers):**
1. guide/07 line 141 says "A refused Codex route request" without a qualifier. A 403 or quota refusal actually becomes a resumable `DECIDER_NOT_AUTHENTICATED` or `DECIDER_RATE_LIMITED` (`events.ts:337-353`; `primitive-evaluator.ts:83-89`). The word "instead" and docs/06's "the same refusal" do tie it to the HTTP 400 case. "The same HTTP 400 refusal…" would be more precise.
2. docs/06 line 521 says "this change does not expand…", which reads like a changelog entry and will date in a design doc.
3. Two older statements fall outside the delta. I'm reporting them only; no action is requested in this slice:
   - ADR-0063 line 32 still says "which no override can weaken". The ADR describes itself as a historical record, and review 1 treated ADR wording that way.
   - guide/07 line 114 says "Correct the node, decision or default" for an inference-only failure code.

## B — #448: ACCEPT CORRECTION

The patch changes only the doc 11 table: 9 lines, of which only the Default model row changes in content and the other eight change padding only. I checked that row against `apps/api/src/preflight.ts`:

| Table cell | Source |
|---|---|
| **ok:** the Codex model is in its enabled catalog, with no effort claim | The model is in the catalog (codex rows) and enabled; effort isn't checked (lines 270 and 283–288). |
| **ok:** the Claude default is the exact supported model and effort | The model is in the catalog, effort is explicit and supported, and the model is enabled (lines 412–425). |
| **warn:** the Codex default is in the catalog but disabled | Lines 280–281. A disabled Claude default is no longer listed as a warning; it fails (lines 417–418). This fixes follow-up 2 from review 1. |
| **fail:** the Codex model is missing | Not found in the codex rows (lines 272–278). That includes an unset Codex model when the setup isn't Ollama-only (lines 367–368; `config.ts:126-130`). |
| **fail:** the Claude default is missing, unknown, wrong-family, disabled, or has an unsupported effort | Lines 413–419. |

"Has unsupported effort" now applies only to Claude. That removes the old row's implication that preflight checks the Codex effort, and the delta adds no new promise about Codex effort. Other doc and guide pages don't contradict the new row. The other parked follow-ups were not pulled into scope.

**Optional wording note (not a blocker):** "Claude default is missing" could be read as "no Claude default is configured". In that case the check doesn't run at all (line 411), and the table's Harness row treats that setup as valid. The fail actually comes from a configured Claude entry whose model isn't in the catalog (line 414). A missing Claude effort also fails (line 415), but the table only implies this through the ok cell. The old row had the same ambiguity, and the parallel wording makes the intended meaning clear. Possible rewording: "a configured Claude default has a missing, unknown, wrong-family or disabled model, or a missing or unsupported effort."

## Limits
- I ran nothing: no git commands, tests, lint, typecheck, format or build. I did not verify parentage or tree SHAs myself; I rely on the brief and the root's capture script. I did not recompute the SHA-256 hashes of the earlier reviews or read the public GitHub comments.
- For A, I checked the runtime claims against the source only. The live QA results (a recognized 400 keeps its reason, a decision gets the generic non-resumable failure, an unknown shape stays uncertain and resumable) are still pending QA.
- I verified the SDK's argument order for flag precedence. How the Codex CLI resolves dedicated flags against `-c` keys internally has not been measured, the same limit as review 1.
- This doesn't claim QA, CI, the final AstraMAX check or owner acceptance. Closing #448 is still the owner's call, and I closed and published nothing.
